request: Analyze GSE155230 for PMID 33193103 (Comparative Analysis of Skeletal Muscle Transcriptional Signatures Associated With Aerobic Exercise Capacity or Response to Training in Humans and Rats.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (Illumina HiSeq 2500, 1x50 bp), rat gastrocnemius
final.primary_estimand: Effect of 8-week treadmill endurance training on gastrocnemius gene expression within each selectively bred trainability line (LRTT vs untrained LRT; HRTT vs untrained HRT), plus the paper's Figure 2 line difference in the trained state (HRTT vs LRTT)
final.sample_inclusion: Generation-15 male HRT/LRT rats; n=3 untrained (HRT, LRT) and n=3 trained (HRTT, LRTT) per line, separate animals (S2.1.3.p1). HCR/LCR samples belong to a separate intrinsic-capacity comparison (case GSE155230_capacity).
planned_contrasts: HRTT vs LRTT (S3.2.p1, Fig 2C; paper: 255 DEGs, 68 up in HRTT, 187 down)
LRTT vs LRT, trained vs untrained low responders (S3.2.p3, Supp Fig 2G; deposited GSE155230_lrtt_lrt_deg: 255 DEGs, 174 up / 81 down)
HRTT vs HRT, trained vs untrained high responders (S3.2.p3, Supp Fig 2G; deposited GSE155230_hrt_hrtt_deg: 90 DEGs, 62 up / 28 down)
HRT vs LRT untrained baseline (deposited GSE155230_lrt_hrt_deg: 234 DEGs, 64 up / 170 down; used in Fig 4E pre-training comparison)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none: trained and untrained rats are different animals (S2.1.3.p1)
final.normalization: Cufflinks upper-quartile normalization, Cuffdiff -b -u (GEO data_processing; S2.3.1.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.1.3.p1 defines four groups of n=3 male rats (untrained LRT/HRT, trained LRTT/HRTT; separate cohorts, not pre/post on the same animals). S3.2.p3 states the exercise-response analysis compares each trained group to its untrained counterpart; this is the within-line training effect, the estimand closest to 'how exercise affects gene expression'. Fig 2C/S3.2.p1 is the headline HRTT vs LRTT contrast (255 DEGs, FC>1.5, FDR<0.05). Exact paper counts for the training contrasts are not stated in the text, so they are taken from the authors' deposited Cuffdiff lists, all of whose rows pass q<0.05 and |log2FC|>log2(1.5) (HRTT/LRTT list reproduces the text's 255 = 68 up / 187 down exactly).

covariates.name: lane
covariates.disposition: not modelled: completely aliased with grp in all four training-case contrasts (HRT L2x3, HRTT L3x3, LRTT L2x3, LRT L3/L1/L1); a sequencing lane inside one GATC run (4266) with libraries prepared in one batch (consecutive lib IDs 99119-99130), not a library-prep batch; its size is checked in the capacity case where it is balanced; recorded as a caveat

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals, no subject blocking; all male (S2.1.3.p1); no batch, age or sex column. Lane (parsed from FASTQ names by prep_counts.py into the metadata copy) is completely aliased with grp for every contrast. Under a strict reading this would stop the case, but lane here is a flow-cell lane of one sequencing run, not a separate library preparation, and technical lane-to-lane variation for RNA-seq is small; the paper's own Cuffdiff results carry the same aliasing. I keep the case and label every training contrast with the caveat; the exploratory lane_check execution in GSE155230_capacity (lane balanced 2:1 within HCR and LCR) measures the lane effect directly.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald), joint model on all 12 samples
